_comment: Guided tour of the native ALEX Suite hub (gui/native.py). It walks the pipeline the way a user does: Load demo data, then Next, Next, Next. Every action step points at the real control (the hub's Next button, the files step's Load demo data) and WAITS for the user to press it (await); nothing is pressed on the user's behalf. Read by chisurf.emtk.help_guide.EmTkGuidedTour.

steps.title: Your old workflow, as one pipeline
steps.text:
The list on the left is ALEX-Suite's workflow: setup, files, microscope settings, burst search, background, corrections, E vs S. Seven numbered steps; below them the tools that were under Advanced Options.

You walk it with Next: each step hands its result to the next one, so from your files to an E–S histogram is a handful of Next presses. The tour points at the buttons; you press them. About three minutes, on a simulated µs-ALEX measurement whose answer is known.

steps.title: 1 — the detector setup
steps.text:
Which routing channels are the donor and the acceptor, and which micro-time window is which excitation. Every later step reads it.

PIE / ns-ALEX: pick or edit your setup here. µs-ALEX (and this demo): leave it; step 3 measures the channels and the laser gates and writes a setup called ALEX Suite (auto).

await.hint: Select 1. Setup in the list on the left.

steps.title: Next walks the pipeline
steps.text: Next runs the open step where it has something to run, waits for it, and opens the next one. >> does that for every remaining step. Steps marked (optional) are never run by Next.

await.hint: Press Next (bottom right) to go to 2. Files.

steps.title: 2 — the files
steps.text:
Drop files or a folder here. .sm files work directly, no conversion, no cache files beside them.

No measurement at hand: Load demo data writes a simulated µs-ALEX stream (100 µs alternation, donor on channel 0, acceptor on channel 1; low-FRET, high-FRET, donor-only and acceptor-only molecules) into a temporary folder and adds it.

await.hint: Press Load demo data in the Summary box.

steps.title: On to the microscope settings
steps.text: The next step is where the old Burst Search Settings → Microscope dialog went: the ALEX period, the phase shift, four laser edges and the channel flip. All seven are in the data.

await.hint: Press Next: the alternation step opens and converts the file on arrival.

steps.title: 3 — measured, not typed
steps.text:
Arriving with µs-ALEX data, this step found the period, the two laser gates and which detector is the donor, folded the alternation into the micro-time (one .pto container beside your file) and wrote the setup. PIE data is left alone.

Check the plot: two plateaus, the donor detector brighter in one, the acceptor in the other. That crossover is what the old channel-flip checkbox was guessing at. The gates are editable here and as bands on the plot.

steps.title: 4 — the burst search
steps.text: The burst search already has the converted file and the setup. One habit worth changing: search permissively and cut on burst size afterwards; a size cut inside the search biases which molecules you ever see.

steps.title: Next runs the search
steps.text: On the burst search, Next runs it, waits until every file is searched, and moves on. The bursts are kept inside the measurement's .pto, and every later step reads them from there.

await.hint: Press Next: the search runs, then 5. Background opens.

steps.title: 5 — the background, measured
steps.text: The bkg_DD / bkg_DA / bkg_AA fields you used to type are estimated here on arrival, from the inter-photon times of your own measurement. Getting them wrong moves E for the dim bursts while the bright ones stay put, which looks exactly like a sub-population.

steps.title: 6 — α, δ, γ and β from your own bursts
steps.text:
The burst table is loaded. Next calibrates: the step classifies donor-only, acceptor-only and FRET bursts, takes α and δ from the single-labelled ones and γ and β from the FRET populations, stores them in the measurement, and opens the E–S histogram, which picks them up.

The check that catches most errors: donor-only must land at E ≈ 0.

await.hint: Press Next: the calibration runs, then 7. E–S histogram opens.

steps.title: 7 — E vs S and the Dataset Viewer, in one
steps.text: ndX shows FRET efficiency against stoichiometry for your bursts: the demo has a low-FRET and a high-FRET population at S ≈ 0.5, and the few donor-only (S ≈ 1) and acceptor-only (S ≈ 0) bursts. Any other burst property can go on either axis, and a region drawn here selects those bursts.

steps.title: Below the line: the Advanced Options
steps.text: Burst properties (the burst table), Titration (a concentration series fitted together, seeded with your bursts and the γ / β of step 6), BVA, and Export (the five CSV files of the old program). They read the same bursts and are not part of the Next walk.

steps.title: Three checks, then believe it
steps.text:
1. The phase plot of step 3 shows the donor/acceptor crossover.
2. Donor-only bursts sit at E ≈ 0 after step 6.
3. The FRET populations do not drift with burst size (plot E against Number of Photons in step 7).

Help (top left) has the full map from the old program's windows to these steps.
